concernsAccepted.finding: Multi-process concurrency on the enqueue→sweep window. DE-9a closes it and is falsification-verified (lock stubbed ⇒ sum(acquired)==2, gate RED), but only for N=2 processes on a single host with a file-based start barrier. NOT proven: N>2 replicas, cross-host contention, or the sweep window under real connection-pool pressure.
concernsAccepted.whyAccepted: Railway runs one uvicorn worker per container, so N=2 exercises the real replica shape; cross-host contention cannot be honestly simulated on one laptop, and pretending otherwise would be worse than declaring the gap.

concernsAccepted.finding: Advisory-lock release is proven only in the lane's test topology. The lane runs one sweep with no competing pool consumer, so the documented residual — another consumer taking the connection between per-lot commits, making the unlock a no-op — is not exercised. The lane BOUNDS the residual; it does not eliminate it.
concernsAccepted.whyAccepted: The lock is efficiency-only by design; the partial unique index uq_coop_ledger_expire_per_lot is the correctness boundary, and it is independently proven by DE-21/G-21. Recorded in the sweep's own docstring and routed to the capacity-hardening advisory-lock audit note via S-27.

findingsRaisedDuringVerification.finding: _EXPIRE_INSERT_SQL ends with ON CONFLICT (lot_id) WHERE entry_type = 'EXPIRE' DO NOTHING. Without the partial unique index uq_coop_ledger_expire_per_lot, PostgreSQL cannot infer an arbiter and EVERY insert raises asyncpg InvalidColumnReferenceError. The mandated per-lot except swallows it, so the sweep completes 'successfully' having expired NOTHING — a silent failure on a billing surface, visible only as coop_expire_lot_failed log spam. Confirmed by mechanism twice (executing agent, then the EVL agent on a disposable Postgres with the index dropped). The index ships in migration b7e4d21a9c58, which has never been applied to production.
findingsRaisedDuringVerification.note: NOT fixed under this phase's blast radius, deliberately. Reported rather than patched in place.

findingsRaisedDuringVerification.finding: The lane's DE-5 gate failed ~7-15% of full-file runs. Root cause was NOT state bleed: _run_job_now() watched next_run_time, which APScheduler advances at job SUBMIT (base.py:1195 submit, :1228-1229 advance), not completion. The test then left the LifespanManager block, and AsyncIOExecutor.shutdown() cancels every in-flight coroutine unconditionally (upstream comment: 'There is no way to honor wait=True without converting this method into a coroutine method'), killing the sweep before its per-lot commit. Measured: sweep 58-250ms against a fixed 250ms poll tick.
findingsRaisedDuringVerification.status: FIXED 2026-08-17 — waits on EVENT_JOB_EXECUTED instead. No retry, no sleep, no flaky marker; the deadline was deleted, not lengthened. 40/40 green; Mutation A (future expires_at) RED proves the assertion still carries signal; Mutation B (revert to sleep) reproduces 2/20 red proving the wait is load-bearing.
findingsRaisedDuringVerification.note: Zero apps/api bytes changed. Production is unaffected and correct: a container shutdown mid-sweep cancels the job the same way, but per-lot commit makes partial progress durable and the next tick resumes — the designed-for case DE-14 already proves.

findingsRaisedDuringVerification.finding: The integration lane carries order-dependent cross-event-loop flakes on the module-level async_session engine.
